utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. This is case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Matthias Neuner and Daryl Mundis, assisted today by Mr. Andres Vatter, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic lead counsel, Stephane Bourgon co-counsel, and Muriel Cauvin legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. On Monday, 7 February 2005, I would like to bid welcome to everybody present in the courtroom; the representatives of the Prosecution, the Defence team of General Hadzihasanovic, the Defence team of General Kubura, as well as the two accused. I do not wish to forget everybody else in the courtroom and outside the courtroom. If there are no issues to raise on the part of the two parties, I'm going to ask the usher to go and fetch the witness, who is probably waiting outside. I'm going to ask the Defence to tell us what is the length of this witness's testimony that they envisage.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence is going to take an hour and a half, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. First of all, let me check whether you hear the interpretation of my words in your language. If that is the case, tell me that you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you, and I can understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have been called as a Defence witness. Before you take the solemn declaration, I would like to hear your first name, last name, the date of birth, and the place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Edin Husic. I was born in Zenica on the 28th of April, 1967.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, what is your current profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a professional soldier. Currently I'm the military attache of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the United States of America.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have a rank? Are you an officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm a colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992 and 1993, did you perform military duties? Were you in a position? Were you attached to any unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was a soldier at the time. I was in the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence of Zenica, and after that I was attached to the command of the 3rd Corps of the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, have you ever testified before, either at an international court or a national court with regard to the events that took place in your country in the year 1992 and 1993 or is this the first time you testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already testified twice before this Tribunal about the events that took place during that particular period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you have already testified, could you please tell us in what cases, and did you appear as a Defence witness or as a Prosecution witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was a Prosecution witness in the Kordic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you have testified twice in the Kordic case or did you also testify in some other case? I can see in the transcript that the interpreter actually tells me in French that you have testified on two occasions. Did you testify on one occasion or on two occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On two occasions in the same case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. So you have testified twice in the same case. I'm now going to ask you to read the text of the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Colonel. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to the Defence lawyers, who are going to conduct their examination-in-chief, I would like to provide you with some information about your testimony. You have already testified before this Tribunal on two occasions, but at the time you were a Prosecution witness. Today, however, you are a Defence witness. The procedure is the same, so our explanations will only confirm what you already know about the procedure. At the beginning, you're going to be asked questions by the Defence lawyers of General Hadzihasanovic, whom you have already met in preparation for this trial. The Defence lawyers have told us that they will need an hour and a half. The questions that you will have to answer form part of the so-called examination-in-chief. Those are the questions which are not leading. They're rather neutral, and it is up to the witness to provide detailed answers to the rather uncomplicated questions. After that, the Prosecution lawyers, seated on your right, will also ask you questions for the duration of an hour and a half. You will soon realise that the character of their questions will be somewhat different than the character of the questions put to you by the Defence lawyers. This procedure is similar to the procedure that exists within the common law system, and the Prosecutor's questions may be somewhat leading in order to get a simple answer from you. Sometimes it will be only a yes or a no. After that stage, the Defence lawyers may take the floor again to ask you additional questions that arise directly from the questions put to you during the stage of cross-examination. And at that moment, if any of the Defence's questions are not directly linked with the Prosecution's questions, they will have to ask permission from the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber, the three Judges seated in front of you, according to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, can also put questions to you at any time. However, for the reasons of convenience, the Judges prefer to wait until the stages of examination-in-chief and the cross-examination are over. The Judges' questions are put to you with two goals in mind: The first one is to clarify your answers; and secondly, the Judges, in the interest of justice, will sometimes want to hear answers from you about the questions that they have in mind. After that, the Judges will allow the Prosecution and the Defence to ask you some additional questions that arise from the Judges' questions. These questions will be put to you either to clarify some answers given by yourself to the Judges or to clarify some of your answers and ask you to provide some more detail. The Judges will never take the floor after that. Last week we explained in written form what was the goal of our questions, and we believe that the explanations that we have provided have addressed the issued raised by the Defence. I would like to inform you of two other important elements. One of them is the fact that you took a solemn declaration, which means that you are not supposed to lie, because this is punishable by law. The second element that I mention before every witness is the fact that a witness may object to making any statement which might incriminate the witness. In that case, when the witness refuses to answer, which is the right which is familiar in the countries where the common law exists, but this is also something that exists at this Tribunal, however, at that point the Chamber may compel the witness to answer the question, and when the witness answers, the Chamber will grant the witness a certain form of immunity. This rule exists in order to help the Trial Chamber to arrive at the truth. It will happen that the parties will present you documents during your testimony. Those documents are most commonly from the military source. They will ask you whether you are familiar with the document and if you can provide any comments about the document. If a question seems too complicated to you, you always have the right to ask the person who has put the question to you to rephrase it. As you know, the Trial Chamber doesn't have any written evidence prior to your testimony, and this is where the weight of your testimony arises from. Your words are very important. Before you there is a screen. Your words are translated into English, and since I believe you speak English, you can follow the translation of your words, your answers given to the questions put to you. For technical reasons, we are obliged to take two breaks during the course of the afternoon, each of them lasting about 25 minutes. These breaks will take place every hour and a half, and it has been foreseen that this session will end at 7.00 in the afternoon. And if the Defence and the Prosecution do indeed take the time that they have indicated to us that they will, your testimony will end today. I'm now going to give the floor to the Defence, who will start their examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Husic.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to what the President of the Trial Chamber has told you, I would also like to ask you to make a pause after my question and only then give your answer. This is required for the translation to be able to proceed smoothly and for everybody in the courtroom to be able to understand you. Did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that you are a professional soldier, Mr. Husic. Where did you acquire your military education, and before the war where did you serve?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I acquired my military education in the former Yugoslav People's Army. From 1982 to 1986, I attended the military grammar school in Belgrade, and then from 1986 until 1989, I was also in Belgrade attending the Military Academy there, and after that I transferred to Pancevo where I attended a specialised course which I completed in 1989. After that, I was assigned to serve in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, did you have a rank, and did there come a time when you left the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Upon completing my education, I became a second lieutenant. A year later, I became a lieutenant, and towards the end of 1991 -- 1991, I left the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, can you tell us why you left the JNA, and after you left it, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I left the Yugoslav People's Army because I did not feel I belonged to that army. I started thinking about going home, and I returned home to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were first hired by the District Staff of the Territorial Defence of Zenica. What was your position in 1992 when you were a member of that staff in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I joined towards the end of April 1992, I joined the Territorial Defence, and in the Territorial Defence Staff in Zenica from the end of June I held the position of the chief for intelligence of that staff, up to the moment when the corps was established, which was at the beginning of December 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the corps was established, did you assume another position, and what duties and tasks did you perform during the course of 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: When the corps was established, I was appointed the officer for intelligence, and later on I became the Assistant Chief of Staff for intelligence in the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that you were the Assistant Chief of Staff. Who was your immediate superior in your capacity as the officer for intelligence?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: When I became the Assistant Chief of Staff for intelligence, my immediate superior was the Chief of Staff of the 3rd Corps, who at the time was Mr. Muradif Mekic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, when you joined the 3rd Corps, what was the make-up of your personnel? What equipment did your service have at its disposal, the service which you first joined as an officer and later on as its head?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: When I arrived there, there were only two of us; my chief at the time, the assistant, Mr. Cikotic Selmo, and myself. And we tried to improve the number of personnel, and after a certain period of time there were only a few of us within that body. Naturally at the very beginning, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I can't say that we didn't have anything, but we didn't have the basics. It was necessary to be able to form units that we could rely on. A reconnaissance company that was part of the corps was subsequently formed, and it was linked to us in professional terms. And a company for electronic reconnaissance, and a counter-electronic combat was formed. There was also a unit of the 3rd Corps attached to the 3rd Corps that was professionally linked to us. And naturally, we tried to bring up to strength subordinate units so that there could be men working on the establishment of a system of intelligence in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, what sort of connections did you have with the superior and subordinate units in order to be able to perform your duties as well as possible at the very beginning, and were efforts made to improve the situation?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: We, at the time, relied on the system of communications that had been established, the system of communications that was used for the superior and subordinate command. We didn't have a special system of communications at the beginning, naturally. The communications with the superior command functioned correctly, more or less correctly given the conditions. So-called packet communications was used. And as far as subordinate units are concerned, one of our tasks was to establish such communications with them. I can't say how rapidly this was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since I would now like to use some documents when examining the witness, I would be grateful if these documents could now be distributed to the Chamber, my colleagues from the Prosecution and, to the other Defence team. And, Mr. President, since I might be using some new documents that the Prosecution has been provided with, and as you are well aware, we have translation problems. These documents, these new ones, haven't been translated. So if I may use them, I will use them in accordance with your instructions. The witness will recognise the document or will not recognise the document, read the relevant part, and if the witness hasn't recognised the document in question, we would just request that the documents be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is how we will proceed as there are no translations. The witness will read the relevant paragraph, the one that you think that is relevant, and the document may subsequently be marked for identification, pending full translation. I believe that you have provided the Prosecution with these documents in good time, and I believe that the Prosecution will be in a position to cross-examine the witness. Mr. Mundis. There are no obstructions to proceeding in this manner? Or Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There are no obstructions so far. We have received a list of P -- or DH numbers, and right now we received the hard copies. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, you mentioned the situation when the body was formed, and you said that you immediately attempted to make the body functional. Please have a look at the document number 1. We only have this document in the Bosnian language. So, Mr. Husic, I would first like to ask you whether you recognise the document before you in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just one small interruption. If I may ask my learned friend to state the DH number or P number of the documents for the record. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I see a number 01819218. Perhaps that is number the number that should be mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the sake of the transcript, I will repeat the number you have just mentioned, Mr. President. The number is 01819218.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, you can see the number at the top of the document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, could you please read out the person who sent the document, the subject of the document, who is it addressed to, and could you read out item 1.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, 3rd Corps Command, Zenica, the 5th of December, 1992. The title of the document is "Seminar For Intelligence Organs Order." It's addressed to all brigade commands, to the Zenica regional staff, to all municipal staffs, to the intelligence organs, the organs mentioned above. It says: "On the basis of demonstrated need and in order to organise and improve intelligence activities, I hereby order: "1. Organise and hold a seminar with all intelligence organs of the above-mentioned commands, staffs, and units on the 9th of December, 1992, on Tuesday, commencing at 0900 hours in the Tehnoprojekt building in Zenica (the 3rd Corps Command) with regard to the subject of intelligence activities in wartime."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the date when this order was issued, tell me whether these activities that started after the establishment of the corps were activities that you were involved in in the course of 1993, too, or rather, what sort of efforts did the 3rd Corps make to ensure that this organ was functioning correctly?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: In the subsequent period, given the way the situation unfolded, it was easy to organise things in this way. It wasn't easy to ensure that the men were outside of their units. Most of the intelligence activities were carried out through orders by requesting intelligence, by submitting reports. So this is the course that the intelligence activities within subordinate units took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registrar has drawn my attention to an issue or a question that I forgot to ask the witness. I'll ask the witness this question immediately. You said that you testified in the Kordic case. When you testified, had you been granted protective measures or not? Did you testify in open session or were protective measures in place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I testified in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, I would now like to ask you to have a look at the documents under the following numbers: 2, 3 and 4. The document numbers are DH578, and then 01820719, 01822418, and P268 under number 5. So documents 2, 3, 4 and 5. And since the first two documents -- the first document has been translated, but as far as document 3 is concerned, and document number 4, could you identify these documents in the same way that you identified the other document? Could you say who sent the document, what the subject of the document is; and in document number 1, could you read out the introduction and item number 1 so that we can see whether you're able to comment on these documents.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, first let me say that document DH0578 is the document that I recognise. This is a document that I drafted. It was sent from the 3rd Corps Command on the 6th of January, 1993, to all brigade commands and the Zenica Territorial Defence District Staff. It's a request for intelligence, form number 1. At the time it was urgent. I don't know if it's necessary to read the entire contents of this document since there is a translation, but this concerns the decisions of the government of the so-called Herceg-Bosna and the order of the Main Staff of the Herceg-Bosna HVO regarding the disarming of the members of the BH army. And we requested that our organs assessed the strength of the HVO in their zones of responsibility and provide this information in reports. We requested that they provide us with this information in code, via couriers or via packet communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, thank you for that answer. Have a look at document number 3, please. The number is 01820719. Who sent the document, what is the subject of the document, and is this one of the documents that have to do with your attempts to ensure that subordinate units were well prepared to carry out the activities you have testified about already?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, let me repeat this. Document 01820719 is also a document that I recognise. It's from the 3rd Corps command. It's -- it was sent on the 9th of April, 1993. It's a request for intelligence information, number 10; and you can see in this document -- since there is no translation I will read it out. "On the basis of reliable information that the HVO is preparing a basis for a new conflict with members of the ABiH or, rather, they're preparing an action to clean up our ranks, in order to prevent such actions and prevent them carrying out their intentions and surprising us, immediately do the following: "1. Intensify intelligence activities with regard to individuals and units from the HVO. "2. Immediately gather information and revise the old disposition of forces and equipment in the territory of the municipality where your units deployed. Provide the intelligence organ of the corps with the information gathered by the 30th of April, 1993, and by 1500 hours. "3. Provide immediate information on anything of importance."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise document 401822418? And if so, could you please read out item 1 in the document.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this document, too, which was sent soon after the previous one, on the 18th of April, 1993, from the 3rd Corps Command. Again it's a request for intelligence information, number 11. It was addressed to all the commands of OGs, brigades, and municipal staffs and to the intelligence organ. It says: "On the basis of their demonstrated need and in order to efficiently provide information, it is necessary to do the following: "1. All information that concerns changes of any information on the force of the HVO should be immediately provided in short and succinct reports."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document 5 now, P268. Since you have said that this is how you provided instructions and in a certain sense trained your intelligence organs and subordinate units, could you now tell me whether this document is one of the documents you used to provide precise instructions on the manner in which one should operate.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: In this case, this is an order for intelligence support. It was sent to the commands of all OGs, to brigades, and municipal defence staffs and to intelligence and intelligence security organs. This document was drafted on the basis of an order from the superior command, which at the time regulated the manner of reporting, the way in which reports were submitted. We had previously established the way in which reports should be compiled and submitted, but given the situation, the superior command requested that the reports have a certain form. So they issued such an order, and it's on the basis of this order that we drafted our own orders for subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, given the documents that clearly show how you requested subordinate units to inform you about any relevant information, and you tried to train them to do this, tell me, how important was it to gather intelligence on the enemy in order to carry out the commander's mission?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It is my personal opinion and my professional opinion that gathering intelligence is extremely important, because without such relevant information on the basis of which one makes assessments, a commander can't take any decisions or, rather, a commander can take decisions, but if we have better intelligence, then the conditions for taking decisions have been improved if a commander has to take such decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, how did you obtain information and intelligence that might have had an impact on the decision-making process in the command at that period?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: During that period, we relied on our reconnaissance units. We also relied on our electronic reconnaissance unit, and within its capabilities we carried out radio reconnaissance because we were not equipped for any other forms of reconnaissance. We also carried out interviews, and we also monitored the local media. This was another way for us to obtain information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, could you please look at document 36. This is another new document. The number is 10/99/3, and the date is 12 January, 19 -- I apologise. The number is 10/288-1. And the date is 23 January 1993. Do you have that document before you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to read, just for the identification of this document, who the -- who drafted the document and when was this document sent, and then I will ask you to read item 4 of this document. Before that, I would like to ask you whether you recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise this document. This is a document issued by the command of the 3rd Corps, numbers 10/288-1. The date is 23 January 1993. This is a report. The number is 21. The intelligence report sent to the staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to be more precise, for the Intelligence Administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at item 4 and read it, and can you tell me whether these were your proposals aimed at preparing your body to be able to carry out such an important mission that was required from it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Item number 4 says: "With regard to this item pursuant -- on the basis of the work so far, with a view to improving organisation and functioning of the intelligence service, we hereby propose that at the level of the command of the corps the intelligence department is established as a special body of the command. The following would -- the following staff would make up this body: Chief officer; two officers for intelligence out of whom one officer, one assistant chief, one younger officer, one typist, translator. The department should be brought to the strength of at least 60 to 80 per cent, and it should have at least one vehicle at its disposal. The intelligence organs in the brigade command Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. should be brought to 100 per cent strength and the same applies to the reconnaissance units at least when it comes to the staff and weapons that they have at their disposal."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you is: Are these proposals of the 3rd Corps sent to the superior command, and how did you by means of such proposals try to prepare your body to carry out its important missions within the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. These were the proposals of the intelligence organ of the 3rd Corps, and the objective was to improve the organisation and functioning of the intelligence service. In any case, we believed that we were not well-equipped and that we did not have enough staff. That is why our proposal showed what we meant the best situation would be when it came to staff. We also said that we needed a vehicle. As far as the subordinate units were concerned, we wanted these to be brought up to the hundred per cent strength, because the customary situation was that there was one person at the level of the brigade and one at the level of each and every battalion, and their reconnaissance units which also were not brought to the full strength, we asked for more attention to be paid to that issue. The situation reflected the situation at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, you have told us that the information that you received from individuals and that -- that was one -- one of your sources of information. Can you please look at documents number 31, 32, and 34. First of all tell me whether you recognise these documents and then I will ask you some questions about these documents. First of all, document after number 31. Tell us, please, who sent it and when, on what date. And the same applies to number 32 and 34.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This is document sent by the command of the 3rd Corps. Number is 10/1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Yes, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we noted that there is no ERN number here on this document. If my learned friend could at least state the date of the document so that later in the transcript the document can somehow be identified. At this moment, it is difficult. This is here transcript lines -- 20, line 1, documents number 31, 32, and 34. If my learned friend could just state the date of the document and where they came from for the record, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is either the Defence or the witness who should provide us with the date of this document that was issued in Zenica. Maybe you could give us the date and the witness could confirm it after you. We have to have that in the transcript, because number 31 does not have any ERN number, so it has to be said that the document originates from the 3rd Corps, that it was issued on the 15th of December, 1992. Maybe we can say that this document bears the internal number of the 3rd Corps, 10/183-1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I can do that. I thought maybe the witness would do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the documents number 10/183-1. The date is 15 December 1992. Then document 10/183-2, and finally the document number 10 dated 11 January 1993. Do you recognise these documents, and what are they about?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise them. I would like to provide separate comments about each of these individual documents. The first one was issued on 15 December 1992. The number is 10/183-1. It is an official record. At the beginning, it says that intelligence organs on the days of the 13 and 14 December 1992 carried out interviews with Merim Galijatovic, father's name Mahmut, born in 1964 in Trebinje, currently residing in Sarajevo in Danila Djekica Street number 28. Currently he is a member of the HVO, and he is an officer of the Siroki Brijeg Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't want to talk about the contents of the document, so you were talking about the way you obtained information. Can you tell us, what does this document represent and how does it reflect the method of your work and the method of collecting information in your service?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: From time to time, we were not in the position to talk to the individuals for whom we assumed that they might provide us with certain intelligence information. In this particular case, we did have such an opportunity, and we took that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at document number 32. The document was issued by the command of the 3rd Corps. The number is 10/183-2, and the date is 20 December 1992. Is this a similar document to the previous one? Do you recognise this document, and can you tell us whether this document is similar to the one and does it reflect the same method of obtaining intelligence information by your service?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this document of the command of the 3rd Corps. The number is 10/183-2, and it was drafted in Zenica on the 20th of December, 1992. Again it's an official record, and again this is an interview that was carried out on that particular date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the same method as the one described in document number 34, the document issued by the 3rd Corps Command under number 10 on the 11th of January, 1993, in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this document. Attached to this document should be an official record. This is report number 10/992. The date is 11 January 1993, and it was sent to the Intelligence Administration of the Supreme Command Staff, and it should contain the official record, which I do not have before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I might have provided you with the wrong document. This is document number 33. However, the document number 34 - this is number 10 - the date is 11 January 1993, and this is an official record. Do you recognise this document, and does it belong to the series describing methods of obtaining information from the physical persons?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is the same type of document. The only number is 10. It was drafted in Zenica on the 11 January 1993. Again it describes another interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to my previous questions, you have told us that you used radio communication that intercepted radio communication, and that's how you obtained information. Can you please look at document number 43, which is a document issued by the 3rd Corps Command, and the number is 10/280-1, and can you tell me, what kind of document is this? Do you recognise it, and whether this was one of the ways that you obtained your information.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document issued by the 3rd Corps Command. The number is 10/280-1. It was issued in Zenica on the 22nd of January, 1993. The title is the Intelligence Report Number 19. It was sent to the Supreme Command Staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to the Intelligence Administration thereof, and you can see in this document how we obtained intelligence. I can read only the first sentence, which says as follows: "Our units for electronic surveillance and anti-electronic fight on the 19th of January, 1993, at 2000 to 2200 hours, during the course of electronic surveillance, the frequency 41.75 megahertz intercepted the following conversation." Then the participants in the conversation are mentioned, and the text is also transcribed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also told us that you collected information from the media and from some documents. Can you please look at document after tab 27. The number is 1387. It does have an English translation. Can you please tell me whether the attachment to this order is one of the sources that you used to obtain information on the behaviour of your enemy?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I can see this document, and in this specific case I was not the author of this document, but you can see that this is an order to prevent surprises and that we analyse a document that the command of the operation zone of Central Bosnia of the HVO sent to its subordinate units, and we forwarded this order to our subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under item 5, you can see that the information that you obtained from this document led to the intensifying of your reconnaissance activities. Tell me, the information that you collected in various ways and by using various methods, did this information govern the work of your intelligence service, or did you have a constant interest in only some subjects of your work?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Given the way the situation developed, this determined where we would focus our activities, and this document shows, and if you bear in mind certain information and the fact that units were requested to intensify the work, well, yes, you can see that this was the case, that they were asked to intensify their work. The activities that they focused on depended on the situation and on whether we had any reliable information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, you have spoken about the structure of the organs and the methods that you used. You mentioned some of the methods that you used. Who did you gather information and intelligence on? Who were you interested in?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: At the time, in 1992, in the course of 1992, we were mainly interested in aggressor forces or, rather, the Republika Srpska forces. However, we were also interested in HVO forces, because occasionally this is how the situation in the field would develop; information was obtained. We didn't consider HVO forces as an enemy, we considered these forces as an ally, but we were interested in them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, could you now tell me, once you had gathered information, your field of work included the situation of the enemy, the Republika Srpska army, and later the HVO, but once you had gathered such information, who would you forward such information and intelligence to? What was the procedure followed when gathering information, assessing information, and forwarding it? Who would you forward your information to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: All the information gathered would first be processed in the intelligence organ. It's very important to make certain assessments when processing the information. Naturally the more information you have or you -- if you get the same information from a number of sources, then the assessment will be better, more appropriate. Once we had made assessments of the information, if we had enough time, if we had enough information, we would then forward this information to the Chief of Staff. If we believed that the information was interesting but we didn't have enough time, we would provide them in the form that we had received such information in, and we would express our opinion that it would be good to have a look at that information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you sometimes provide information to subordinate units too?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. We soon started to inform our subordinate units too. In this case, we informed our colleagues, our colleagues in the intelligence organs, and it was their duty to inform their superiors, and this was one of the ways of informing them, of focusing our work. This enabled them to know what was happening. This enabled them to make certain assessments and to be well-informed. And this certainly improves the pre-conditions that required for them to continue with their work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you about who your organ was interested in, you said that in 1992, you were interested in the Republika Srpska army, which was the aggressor, but you said that you also started gathering information and assessing information on the HVO. Tell me, why did you become interested in the HVO, and when did you realise that it was necessary to view the HVO not only as an ally but also someone who perhaps didn't share the same objectives as the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, we were interested in the HVO above all because of the situation that prevailed at the time in territory that was under the control of the HVO or that was administered by the HVO. As an example, we were interested in them because in the territory under HVO control, there was limited control of movement, but certain other things took place. Our members would be arrested, inhabitants would be arrested. So in order to prevent certain things from happening, it was important to have information. But this wasn't a matter of priority for us and it varied from situation to situation. However, there were also certain indicators showing that HVO members were establishing contact with the enemy, with the Republika Srpska army at the time, and naturally we thought it was necessary to pay attention to this. So there were incidents, of course. The first time we thought that a serious conflict was breaking out with HVO units was in mid-January in Gornji Vakuf. After those events, we focused our attention on the territory where HVO units were deployed or, rather, on territory under HVO control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, you said, "We considered the HVO to be an ally." Did you obtain any information on how the HVO viewed the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, from time to time we would hear in conversations, in interviews, or in certain cases we would come across certain documents, and this was particularly the case when the organs of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna were being established. They were, in fact, establishing control over that territory. So bearing all this in mind, we believed that a state was being created within a state, and we had certain information to this effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, please have a look at document number 7, number 0556, and please have a look at item number 1. The HVO says that the enemy forces of the ABiH should be broken up and certain places are mentioned. Tell me, does this first item, once you have read it, reflect the information that you had in January 1993 on how the HVO began to view the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This document, 0556, was drafted by the Operative Zone of North-Western Herzegovina. The number is 01/35-1, Tomislavgrad, the 12th of January, 1993. The title of the document is Action of the Operative Zone of North-Western Herzegovina Forces in Gornji Vakuf and Bugojno. It's an order addressed to all brigades in this Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read it out to yourself and then answer my question, because we do have the English version of this document. The Chamber and my colleagues in the courtroom have the English translation of this document so you don't have to read it out loud, but please have a look at it and tell me if it reflects the information you had on how the HVO was behaving in January 1993 in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The document shows, and in particular item number 1 shows the following: It says that the attack forces of the operation zone and other Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. forces, which were probably in the zone, it says that they are to rout the enemy forces, and in the brackets it says the BH army in Bugojno and Gornji Vakuf. One can see what the objective is. If I continue, I can see that it mentions certain tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not necessary, Mr. Husic. All I'm interested in is whether this document reflects the information you had on the way in which the HVO was behaving in January 1993 in the Central Bosnia area.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we didn't have this document. We didn't have such precise information -- or, rather, we couldn't have expected that they would really carry out an attack against us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at document number 8 now. 0571 is the number on the top of the document. And tell me -- or, rather, have a look at this document and then have a look at document number 9, 0575. Document number 12, 0587. And once you have had a look at these documents, could you tell me whether these documents also confirm the information that you had at the time, the information that you had on the HVO was no longer an ally and had started behaving in a completely different way. Have a look at these HVO documents and then could you please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Document 0571 is similar to the previous document, and here it says that Colonel Siljeg should be informed that the Muslims deliberately negotiating all the time while they're simultaneously being active on the front line. This is their tactic. It says, "Order our forces to open fire." So, yes, they are treating us as an enemy here. And then you mentioned number 10; is that right? Twelve?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I said number 10.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Number 10, 0580, from the 3rd Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 9. I apologise. 0575. And number 12.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: 0575 is also an order from the Bobovac HVO Brigade, dated the 16th of January, 1993. And in the introduction, it mentioned certain things that are not true; that we carried out an attack, et cetera, and that they are placing their units in a state of readiness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at document number 12 now. Could you tell me whether this document also reflects the situation you were familiar with on the basis of the information you had in January 1993. The information you had on the way the HVO was behaving, was this the reason for which you focused your attention on HVO units?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: In document 0587 from the Bobovac Brigade, the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion Haljinici, dated the 17th of January, 1993. This is an order again. It also has to do with combat readiness of units and ensuring that they have maximum ability. Certain tasks are being set. It reflects the situation at the time, and this is one of the reasons for which we decided to monitor HVO activities and to monitor them more intensively than before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, you had a look at a number of HVO documents that mention how the ABiH should be treated. Have a look at document number 10 and document number 11 now, and could you tell me whether you recognise these documents and do they reflect the information you had at the time on the way in which the HVO was behaving?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The document number 10 is 0580. This document was issued by the 3rd Corps Command, and it was sent to the intelligence administration of the Supreme Command Staff. It's an intelligence report based on which one could see that we did have certain intelligence regarding the HVO and its units. For example, on page 1 you can see, under section 474, it says here on the basis of the new information of the HVO in Cajdras, Grahovcici --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the witness could slow down reading this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read -- look at the second page and the whole section thereof. And you don't have to read it. We have a translation. And can you tell me whether this was the information that you had at your disposal at the time, and was that part of your intelligence that you reported on in your reports?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is an intelligence report, and again we're talking about the intelligence that had to do with Zenica and Vitez, Novi Travnik as well. This report talks about units which had arrived, and they didn't belong to that area of responsible. This is something that reflects the situation at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Husic, when did the relationship with the HVO deteriorate further? When did you intensify your work in order to enable the 3rd Corps Command to perform its mission and take appropriate measures?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The intensity of our work depended on the development of the situation. However, from that period of time onwards, we continued monitoring the HVO. As far as I can remember, the next serious conflict took place in the sector of Vitez after the attack on the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you to look at document number 14. The number is 18 -- 1782. Tell me whether this was a period of particularly intensive intelligence gathering regarding the behaviour of the HVO. Was that something that you paid particular attention to? But not only you but also the other organs of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Did you say number 14?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, number 14. And the number that it bears is 1782.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This number 1782 is actually a document issued by the HVO in Vitez, and the date is 16 April 1993. It is engagement in further combat operations. We can assume that this is an order, because this is the style and the tone of this document. And especially in its item 1 in which it says: "Capture the villages of Donja Veceriska, Ahmici, Sivrino Selo and Vrhovine completely."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time did you have ample intelligence on the activities of the HVO or its offensive in the area where the units of the 3rd Corps were active?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: At the time we did have certain information. However, I can confirm that we did not have information that there would be this attack on behalf of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, maybe this is a good time for our first break. If the Trial Chamber will allow me to do so, I will ask the witness to look at the remaining documents. I am going to group these documents according to the subjects that I'm going to tackle. It will enable me to proceed with my examination-in-chief without asking the witness to read in front of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We shall now take a break. We shall resume around ten past four. The witness is allowed to peruse the binder and thus will save the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, before the break we were talking about the HVO activities in April. During that period of time, did you face with the propaganda which aimed at distorting the facts of the events that were taking place in the area to what extent your information had -- had a bearing on the mission of the 3rd Corps Commander?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were faced with this propaganda. Whatever was going on was accompanied by propaganda activity. However, from the intelligence point of view, we could only observe that. But this was not our method of work. We monitored the media in order to obtain data, to obtain information that might point to what would follow. There was a lot of propaganda, obviously, but there is nothing else I could say about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was not going to discuss propaganda with you in any case. However, you did say that the information that you received after the events in the Lasva Valley and in Ahmici and its impact. I would kindly ask you to look at document 16. The number is 0866. Can you please look at the first sentence and tell me, was this the best way in which the general public was informed of the events at -- the customary way the events were portrayed totally different than they actually looked?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: What we can see here is that they accused us of the attack. We know what happened there. We were always called Muslim forces, and this was part of that propaganda. We were not Muslim forces, as is well known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was a document issued by the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna. The number is 01-4-264/93, the date is 16 April 1993. Let's move on to another subject. The subject is whether in the situation in which the mission of the 3rd Corps was carried out and the mission was the state defence. Were you faced with the information on the cooperation between the two enemy forces that the BiH army was in conflict at the time? If you have that information, when was the earliest information that you received on this cooperation?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: As I've already told you, the HVO became a subject of our interest before these conflicts in Gornji Vakuf, which were a real turning point. Even before that, we had information that there was a contact between members of the HVO and Republika Srpska army that we considered our enemy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at document number 30. The number -- the document was issued by the Supreme Command Staff of the armed forces. The number is 02347 -- 173. And can you please tell me whether you have any personal information about the contents of this information, especially its first paragraph. The number of the document is 1468. It's a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: One can see from this document that it arrived from the Supreme Command, from the superior command. However, it says in the first sentence that according to the report of the intelligence organ of the regional staff of Zenica, and so on and so forth. The negotiations in Teslic are mentioned. Some names are mentioned. If I were to see my own report, I could confirm all this. However, this document is something that I'm familiar with, and I know the person who authored it because he was my superior along the professional lines of command in my superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, on the 24th of September, 1992, who was the head of the intelligence organ of the regional staff of defence of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I was the head of the intelligence organ at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell me, please, what was the importance of the information on cooperation between the two enemy forces when it came to the mission of the corps commander? How did it impact the situation in your area? Was the situation even more compounded by that cooperation?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The information was anything but welcome. Our situation was anything but enviable at the time, and this cooperation was anything but welcome. On the other hand, we found this behaviour rather strange. We tried to confirm whether this was really the case. We had some previous experience from -- with the HVO, and we didn't know why this happened. However, later on it turned out that there indeed was cooperation between the HVO and the Republika Srpska army. This compounded the situation even further, and the situation after that deteriorated rapidly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your intelligence and the real situation on the ground, you realised that the HVO and the army of Republika Srpska engaged in a joint fight against the BiH army. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The most obvious example was Zepce, and this fully confirmed our information. We had an opportunity to see units of the Republika Srpska army and HVO units acting in concert and fighting together. This was the most obvious example of direct cooperation between the two forces. Although we had some previous intelligence, this is the classical example of the intelligence being confirmed in practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you to look at the documents after the title number 3, Cooperation Between The HVO and The Republika Srpska Army. Look at documents after number 48 to number 59 and tell me, please, whether these documents -- actually, look at documents up to number 60. When you look at these documents, would you say that they confirmed your intelligence on permanent cooperation and the development of that cooperation between the two enemies against the BiH army? If you think that any of the documents among these should be highlighted and commented upon, please do so. I am going to ask you to look at all of them, and I'm going to quote their numbers. After 48, the number of the document is 0651. After tab 49, the number of the document is 1192. On tab 50 we have 1260. On tab 51 we have 1280. On tab 52 we have 1291. On tab 53 we have 1309. On tab 54, we have 1340. On tab 55, we have 1335. On tab 56, we have 1339. On tab 57, we have 1380. On tab 59, we have 1542. On tab -- tab 59, we have 1542. I hope you had an occasion to skim through these documents during the break. Now I would kindly ask you to answer the following question: Do these documents issued by the HVO confirm your information in 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Certainly. I would like to start --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please hold on just a second. The Prosecution has a remark.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just a correction for the record. It is on page 36, line 1. Two, there's twice 1542 mentioned, but I think my learned colleague wanted to say 1543. Can this please be corrected for the transcript please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The first document, number 0651, as far as I can tell this followed the events in Gornji Vakuf. It was drafted by the Main Staff of the HVO, and in item 1 it says that the defence line facing the Chetniks should be weakened to the minimum. They obviously lost any interest in engaging the Chetniks. The next document, 1192, the date is 16th of June. It was issued by the Zepa Brigade, 111.XP Brigade. I found here that in one place a reference is made -- let me just try and find it. On line 15, it says that Serbs with the commander of the Doboj OG, Colonel Arsic, offered full cooperation in joint fight against the balija in these areas. They also request from us an urgent response about that cooperation. "We are in two minds. We need your opinion very urgently. We don't want to further the same as Travnik." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Who are balijas?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This is another term, a derogatory term that was used in the propaganda vocabulary and what they meant are the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The next document is 1260, and it was issued by the same brigade on the 26th of June, 1993. It says here that, "Due to the aggression of the Muslim forces, we were forced to abandon the defence line and the positions facing the Serbian army." The facilities are mentioned here, and it says that the Serbian army respects the cease-fire, and they have not engaged or opened fire against the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the positions were surrendered to the Serbian army. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says. "We were forced to hand over, to surrender our positions," which means that they ceded their positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the following document, number 1280. Again at the end of item 1, it says: "Enemy." It says, "In the course of the day the Serbian forces infiltrated tanks through our territory, and they're preparing to take Zavidovici, and Maglaj and Tesanj have been completely encircled and will not be able to withstand the blockade for very long." It's obvious this refers to cooperation between the HVO and the Republika Srpska army. The next document, 1291, it's from the security service from Vitez, and as far as I have understood, they are analysing a situation. At the beginning it says about establishing contact with representatives of the Serbian army, with responsible representatives of the Serbian army, and then it also says, "From all information available you can see that there's been numerous contact between HVO individuals and individuals from the Serbian army." And then certain other details are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can have a look at the next document.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: If I may, I think that this document suggests developing similar contacts in that area, so to speak. The following document, 1309, it's the North-Western Herzegovina area. The staff is issuing an order to provide documents to those brigades and to provide coordinates and a list of MOS objectives that have to be targeted. "XY side," it says. And at the end of the sentence it mentions the line that MOS is holding in direction of the Serbs. The Serbian army, the Republika Srpska army is the XY side here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this is an HVO document, could you please say who the HVO call the MOS.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The MOS is an abbreviation for the Muslim armed forces, and naturally in this case they consider the ABiH to be the Muslim armed forces. The next document is from the same command. It's to the commander personally. It says that a report should be provided on Chetnik activities in the morning and on the targets that they fired at. And then there's a handwritten part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document 56 now. 56, 57, and 59. I think that would be enough in order to clarify the problem that you were confronted with when performing your duties as well as the 3rd Corps Command when performing its mission.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This document relates to what I've already been testifying about. It -- it mentions the army, the red, and there's other information on agreements, and then it says -- at the end there's a post script and it says, "Tell the Serbs that their people are together with our people and that the Serbs are fighting the Muslims alongside our forces and that's how the Serbs have been killed." The next document is document 1380. This is dated August 1993, and it is about the efforts made by the XP Brigade to establish contact with the 110th HVO Brigade with which we were not in a conflict. It behaved in a correct manner, so to speak, complied with its duties, and it mentions the meeting at Teslic, and we know that that was in territory under the control of the Republika Srpska army. And this document is about the efforts made in order to get this unit involved. And what was the other document you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: 59. The date is the 18th of November 1993. I think the document number, the next document is 1542 and it says, on the basis of an agreement between the Republika Srpska government and the Herceg-Bosna government, two tanks were leased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've had a look at a lot of HVO documents and you've read through them. Tell me now, Mr. Husic, you've commented on all these documents, and do these documents confirm the information that you had in 1993 on the cooperation of two enemy forces? And tell me, in 1993, what sort of a situation was the 3rd Corps Command in as far as performing its mission was concerned?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Having had a look at these documents, naturally this confirms the information that we had. These documents contain a lot of information that we were not aware of at the time. But in any event, this information does support the idea that there was cooperation and that this cooperation had started even earlier, in the territory of Bugojno. So what could the situation have been like if we had been totally encircled? Well, I wouldn't comment on that, but it couldn't have been worse, most likely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, could you please just have a look at documents number 60, 1124; 61, the number of this document is DH1130. Document 62, the number of this document is DH1140; and number 63. Can you tell me whether these documents from the Republika Srpska army confirmed the information that you had, and do they confirm the sort of situation that the 3rd Corps had to go through, live in in 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The first document, 1124, under item 1 mentions the firing support of HVO forces. Item 2 mentions taking care of wounded. So, yes, this is a textbook example of cooperation, and the document does confirm this. The next document, number 1130, which was drafted on the following day, we can see that they're regulating the status of HVO prisoners in the Travnik sector. The first part says that they requested that lines be taken and that they should be taken care of until a final solution had been found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That document is already in evidence, but my question is when you have a look at the following document, at the time the documents drafted by the Republika Srpska army, did these documents confirm what you knew in -- within your body? Did it confirm -- do these documents confirm the information that you had in your organ?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. This document, which is from the corps command, provides instructions to the Vlasic OG. And in the previous documents I have spoken about, in the previous document, cooperation was already mentioned. It referred to regulating the status. And the following document you have mentioned says, according to the information we have -- well, the document is DH1140. I think the office of the president of Republika Srpska forwarded this to the Main Staff, and it says that he is ordering soldiers in Serb territories on Vlasic. It says they have to be transported to Vares with all of their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Awhile ago you said that sometimes your sources of information were not very reliable and the media were not very reliable. Have a look at the last document. In spite of what you said, in the ABiH were you aware of the fact that this cooperation and everything else that took place in 1993 was in fact part of something that had been agreed upon far earlier, or were you not aware of that at the time? Did you have no such information at the time? This is document 63. It's a press release dated the 7th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: At the time, we didn't have this document. The date is May 1992. But when I have a look at this document, it's clear that agreements were reached at a high political level, and it was said that Bosnia would be separated into three -- or divided into three independent states. So this does confirm that. But we hoped that in spite of all information that we had, this would not happen, because to this very day I don't understand why, given everything that people had been through in Croatia, I didn't understand why the HVO was fighting us. I didn't understand why they wanted this, why we weren't allies, which is what we should have been at the beginning, because so many of our men fought in the Republic of Croatia too. And on the other hand, there were quite a lot of men, especially in Herzegovina, there were quite a lot of men in the HVO units. So we had information, but we hoped that none of this would happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, just a few more questions that have to do with the second field in which you were active in 1993. In mid-1993, were you assigned to any other duties in the 3rd Corps Command; and if so, can you tell us what sort of duties you were assigned?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: From time to time, I was also engaged as liaison officer. Above all, I had to liaise with BritBat. There were so many international organisations present there. There was a lot of pressure to establish contacts. Those were duties that I was assigned, although later one of the intelligence organs of the 3rd Corps continued with that work. But during that period of time, these duties had to do with meetings at high levels, at levels that -- where I wasn't usually present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, with regard to that role, what policies did the 3rd Corps pursue as far as assisting international organisations is concerned, and primarily UNPROFOR, so that they could perform their mission unhindered, the mission for which they were in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: We tried to help them as much as possible to ensure that they could perform their mission. That was the -- those were the policies pursued by the 3rd Corps. We tried to grant all their requests. And when I had contact with these bodies, it was my task to act in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, tell me, to what extent did Commander Hadzihasanovic, when he had contact with UNPROFOR representatives and representatives of international organisations, to what extent did he contribute to pursuing these 3rd Corps policies and implementing them?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, since I received instructions from the Chief of Staff, on the whole, as far as I know, General Hadzihasanovic, at least when I had contact with him, was positive and responded in a positive manner to requests for meetings. And deputy -- his deputy, General Merdan, was in fact responsible for such contact because there were so many agreements, so many negotiations at that time, and representatives of the international organisations were always involved in these negotiations and agreements. So he was the main person for such contact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Husic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This concludes my examination-in-chief, and I apologise for having taken up ten additional minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now turn to the other Defence team. Do they have any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. At this point in time, Mr. Kubura's Defence has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Prosecution may commence with their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before I commence with the cross-examination, I would just point out that there is one new document which has been disclosed to the Defence, to both Defence counsels yesterday at noon. So within the 24-hour -- or more than 24 hours in advance. And this document is authored by today's witness, and for this reason I'm anticipating that I'm showing this today. Cross-examined by Mr. Neuner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Husic. My name is Matthias Neuner, and I am appearing on behalf of the Prosecution here, and I want to ask you some questions. If you don't understand my questions, please ask me to repeat or rephrase them and I will try to do so. You just testified in extenso about the cooperation between the VRS and the HVO in Central Bosnia in 1993. Do you agree with me that even if such cooperation between the HVO and the VRS was occurring, this in no way could affect the principle duty of the corps commander, Mr. Hadzihasanovic, or of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, Mr. Kubura, to prevent crimes of their own subordinates in 1993? Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: They certainly had an impact on all the decisions made by the commander. I'm talking about the crimes that were committed, but I cannot say that this did not have an impact. In any case, this compounded the situation. I wouldn't be able to agree with you on the position that you have just put forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. You said you cannot say that this did not have an impact. Can you try to explain why and how should it have an impact on the commander's duty to prevent crimes if adversaries might cooperate? Isn't the duty to prevent an overall duty, the duty to prevent crimes?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Certainly. There is a duty to prevent crimes. It's a key duty. However, when the situation is complicated, I'm sure that your decisions are affected by that. If we're talking about how these decisions were affected, it's very simple. If the situation had not been such as it was, these units would have been engaged in a certain other area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you agree with me that the units who were fighting the enemy are distinct from the units who have to prevent crimes? I'm talking about ABiH units now.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Your question is rather general and broad. Can you be more precise? In my view, units are units. They have a certain purpose. Could you be more specific in your question and narrow it down a little?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to the complexity of the situation at the time in 1993 and that the complexity of the situation could have an impact, in your opinion, on the duty to prevent. What I try to get at is to ask you which unit -- which units within the 3rd Corps had to prevent crimes, and didn't this -- these units have this specific task as opposed to combat units who were -- whose task it was to fight the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am trying to understand the questions by my learned friend, but these questions are not for me but for the witness, and I fully appreciate that. However, within the scope of my examination-in-chief, I was not talking about units that were involved in crime prevention. We're talking about the intelligence organ, about the intelligence and information that that organ had. And if these questions do not serve to refresh the witness's memory or to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. discredit the witness, they certainly do not arise from any of the questions that were put to the witness during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.
