I believe that on page 24, line 18 and 19, the witness told us exactly what he did, and he was involved in the -- in collection of the intelligence on the HVO and the aggressor forces, and there was no mention of the crime prevention units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has mentioned a number of problems. The first one mentioned by Mr. Kubura's Defence -- I will give you the floor. I will summarise the position of both Defence teams. The lawyers of General Kubura have just told us that the witness has not spoken about any units that might have committed crimes, that his main activity, the chief activity was to collect information on the relationship between the HVO and the Serbs and the consequences that this relationship might have had on the BiH army. The other Defence team, representing General Hadzihasanovic, have mentioned that they have not addressed this type of problem in their examination-in-chief. I would like to hear from the Prosecution why they are asking this type of question. At my level, I have not been able to understand the meaning of your questions and why you're putting those questions to the witness. Either you are putting the questions that nobody understands, or you have an explanation for those questions. Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution is moving on, Your Honours, to another line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, to the best of your recollection, did any contacts between the ABiH and the Serbian side, the VRS, occur in 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The intelligence organ did not have such information. I personally can say that one could hear and that there were rumours on such contacts, that there was trade going on and so on and so forth. However, I wouldn't be able to provide you with any comment whatsoever, because I personally do not know, nor was I in the position to see any such information, to have such information at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just mentioned rumours, and my learned colleague has shown you a document. This is in your binder, number 52, or tab 52, and it's DH1291. If you could please have a look at this document. It's an HVO document dated 7 July 1993. And if you please look at the third or the second paragraph, starting with "Postoje..." In English it's indeed the third paragraph, starting with "There's also information indicating..." In the B/C/S version it's the passage with "Postoje..." Do you find this passage? If you could maybe read out this one sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: You will confirm whether this is the exact sentence: "There is also information indicating that the Serbian side maintains similar contacts with representatives of the BiH army only the BiH army had definitely been better prepared. Given the overall relations --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much. I understand -- or I understood from your answers that this is an HVO document, but you commented upon it while it was shown to you. Do you have any idea what this can refer to here?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Comment was required from me, and I provided it. From what I can see here, the next sentence speaks about the evaluation by this body, and it says here: "Given the overall relations existing in the area, we estimate that the contacts between the Serbian army and the HVO are pretty realistic, especially since some of our agreements have been implemented in practice (the area of Zepce, the crossing of Mt. Vlasic...)" and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to comment upon the next sentence, I'm actually asking you to comment upon the one sentence which you read out. I understood also from your earlier response that the document relates in part to cooperation between VRS and HVO. I'm just asking you now to tell the Trial Chamber whether you know anything about cooperation between ABiH and VRS as stated in this sentence, for example.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: In my previous testimony, I looked at a number of documents which spoke about the information that we had. And as I analysed all that information and as I looked at some other documents, I can confirm that there was such cooperation and that it reached the level of cooperation or concert activity, joint fighting. I'm talking about the HVO and our -- the army of Republika Srpska fighting together against the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is it, if that's what you're asking me about. However, if you're asking me about the first sentence, I said I don't know anything about that. I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I move on to another topic. Please just state for the record the date on which you were appointed assistant commander for intelligence within the 3rd Corps. You mentioned you were appointed, but when were you appointed?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I really don't remember the exact date, but this should have been at the beginning of December 1992. This is when I was assigned to work in the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From -- in December 1992, did you also -- did you already become assistant commander for intelligence or did you acquire that post at a later point in time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: No, not at first. I was appointed later because there was already an assistant, the officer who had been appointed to that post, and I have already said that. The assistant -- the Assistant Chief of Staff for intelligence at that time was Mr. Selmo Cikotic. I was just an officer in that service, in that organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you substitute Mr. Cikotic in the post of assistant commander for intelligence in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I believe that this was -- I would actually stand in for him every time he was absent. When he was appointed the commander of the OG, and before that he was a member of the negotiation team for the negotiations that took place in Gornji Vakuf, it was after that that I was appointed. Before that, I stood in for him every time he was absent. I was the acting assistant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I understand that after negotiations in Gornji Vakuf, you were appointed. Can you just state at least a month? When were these negotiations in Gornji Vakuf? When were they taking place, and approximately what point in time were you appointed?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It was in January, as far as I can remember. I was appointed in March, I believe. I really can't give you the exact date. If you were to provide me with the order, this would still not reflect the real situation because I was appointed a bit later than I actually started performing these duties as the acting assistant for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. You were referring to March in the sense of March 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. However, I was there all the time. I was a member of this intelligence organ, and I was engaged in these duties all this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The subordinated intelligence departments in the operation groups and within the brigades, would these intelligence organs exclusively report to the 3rd Corps intelligence department, or could they alternatively send information further up the chain of command to the Supreme Command of the ABiH and thereby bypassing the 3rd Corps? Can you please explain.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The chain of command and control at that time was very precise. Generally speaking, when we're talking about any army, a subordinate unit sends its report to the superior command. In the specific case, all the intelligence organs, be it in the OG or the brigade, report within its own unit to the Chief of Staff and the commander, and they also have their own line according to which they send reports to their superior command, from the brigade to the corps command. As far as I know it was never requested from the subordinate command to report directly to them. The information reached us first. I'm talking about the intelligence line. And then when we received information, we would forward that information to the administrative -- to the Intelligence Administration that was above us in the chain of command. It was part of our superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the intelligence organs from the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade submit intelligence reports to your unit?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned during your testimony - it was page 9 of today, I think - that reconnaissance companies of the 3rd Corps were formed. Can you describe what the reconnaissance company -- what the tasks of such a reconnaissance company is and when it was formed, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: These units were established immediately after the 3rd Corps was established. I cannot tell you exactly when these units were formed. However, when the order was issued to establish the corps, this was followed by the order to establish its units amongst which the reconnaissance company, which was a unit attached to the corps staff. The of this unit, the primary task of this unit, was to reconnoiter, to collect information on the enemy, and very often, generally speaking, these reconnaissance units were also used as combat units. In other words, not only for the specific tasks of a reconnaissance unit, which reflected the situation very well. I would have been much happier if that unit could only do its proper job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the commander of this reconnaissance company of the 3rd Corps, and where was the unit stationed?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the name of this unit's commander. For a period of time, this unit was stationed in a building close to the Raspotocje mine near Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the commander of that unit, did this commander report to the assistant commander of intelligence? To whom did this commander report to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: He reported to us if he -- if the unit performed tasks on our orders. If this unit was resubordinated to some other unit, then he didn't report directly to us but he reported through the chain of command to his first superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can -- if you can please look at tab 5 of the list of Defence documents which was given to you. This is a document P268. You have already commented upon that document. If you look at the very last page, please, of this document. On the left-hand side you find initials, "HE/HE" there. Do you find this? Tab 5 of the Defence documents.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Document 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have provided already the details. It's P268. If you can just look at the last page where on the left-hand side two initials, HE and HE, can be found, HE/HE. The last page of the document behind tab 5.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Number 5. Yes. 01853885 is the number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... can you please just answer my question. On the last page you find initials HE/HE there. Does this refer to you, to your person?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Since this is an order for intelligence support, yes, it probably refers to me too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So HE standing for Edin Husic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That stands for Edin Husic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look now, there are two forms attached -- contained in this document. If you look at the first form, and this is actually page 2 of the B/C/S and of the English version, and if you look at number 4(A). There is the possibility to resubordinate organs. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can please inform the Trial Chamber, which organs can the brigades or the OGs request, according to this form, to be resubordinated? Which organs are envisaged here?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Above all, reference is made to what we had at our disposal in the unit or, rather, in the staff above the unit requesting such resubordination. So they could have requested that a platoon be sent to them in territory -- in that territory, a platoon from the reconnaissance company, for example, or to have our company for electronic reconnaissance and electronic jamming engaged, because they're contacting us in this particular case as the superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reconnaissance company of the 3rd Corps or the electronic reconnaissance unit would be then sent to the requested unit in 1993? Did this occur on a continuous basis?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, if someone had made such request, then the commander in the corps would have to see whether we were in a position to grant such a request. Naturally this is the form of the request, but this was not used. Usually a unit would really be resubordinated as a combat unit. That's what happened in the greatest number of cases. But in such cases the request would not be forwarded by the intelligence organ, and sometimes there were no requests at all but the commander would just decide that one of the units should be resubordinated or sent as reinforcements to the area in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you -- we just dealt with the question from the first report. If you now stay within this document and look to the weekly intelligence report. This is question number 2(H). This is on page 3 of the B/C/S document and page 4 of the English version. I'm referring to question 2(H). Do you find this paragraph 2(H)? And mention is made there of "psychological propaganda against our forces."

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: If I can ask you, the psychological propaganda mentioned, did this questionnaire here envisage allegations made by the HVO, for example along the lines that the HVO would use Mujahedin during their combat operations or would use Mujahedin in their territory or would have Mujahedin on their territory? What was this psychological propaganda? What is -- what is meant by this? Please explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is a form, as the witness has said, a form that was provided to all units. This document doesn't mention any of the subjects referred to by my learned colleague from the Prosecution, and this is not something that the witness has testified about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the party putting questions can ask the person who drafted the document what he meant by "psychological propaganda." He could perhaps provide certain explanations about what was meant in the field. Is this just an empty term that doesn't mean anything or did it have a certain sense? Colonel, you have heard the question. Could you answer the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. question put to you. When you wrote down "psychological propaganda," what did this mean? This is the question that the Prosecution is putting to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, by this term I meant anything that might have an effect on our units and on the population. Usually the purpose of propaganda is to disseminate information that will give rise to doubts, that will make the population of the units suspicious or doubt what they're doing, have doubts about what they're doing, or might make them change the way they thought. So under (H) when it -- well, the organs, if they had such information, would also have to provide information about this subject. I think that this is quite clear, in my opinion. But if you would like me to provide you with further explanations, I'll try to provide you with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive such a weekly report back mentioning in this area of the report the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I don't believe so, or I can't remember. If you could show me a document, I'd be happy to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified earlier about the sources of intelligence to my learned colleague. You mentioned the reports you received from subordinated organs. You mentioned that electronic means were available to tap phones, the intercepting of mails, and you also mentioned - that is on page 17, line 23 - that interviews were carried out to collect intelligence information. Can you please tell us who in your unit was involved in such interviews and where they took place. Who was interviewed? Can you please inform us a little bit.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, on page 17, line 23, does this relate to some of the documents or to what I have already been speaking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have the page now in front of me, but I assume you -- this is the transcript. This is the transcript which is in the proceeding. It is now page 56, so it means probably half an hour, maybe an hour ago. You just mentioned interviews were carried out, and I wanted to ask you what you had in mind here. Who did the interviews? Who was interviewed? If you can enlighten us, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, we had proof that such interviews had been conducted. There were official records, et cetera. These documents show that I conducted these interviews. Perhaps there were others as well. In other cases, if we had documents, I could comment on it. There wasn't just one person. We did what was possible at the time, and if we had information or if it was possible for us to interview someone. Our task as an intelligence organ wasn't to conduct interviews of all kinds, it was only to conduct interviews if this was of interest for intelligence reasons and if we had information that might be useful to have an interview with someone. If I can comment on something else. As far as tapping phones is concerned, we really didn't have such equipment, although in one case we did tap a phone, and this is something I have testified about. I testified about this earlier. But as far as monitoring radio conversations is concerned, well, yes, we monitored conversations that were held over the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming back to the interviews. You said that you conducted some interviews. Did you conduct these interviews in your own office or did you go somewhere in the field, to somewhere in the field in order to conduct the interviews?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I think I conducted all the interviews in my office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the persons who were interviewed, were these civilians? Were these prisoners of war? Can you please tell us where these people were coming from. Were they coming from a detention facility? Just asking.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, the people who were interviewed came on a voluntary basis. The intelligence organ wasn't responsible for prisons of any kind, and this isn't how we did our work. It is true that later on in certain cases interviews were conducted with POWs too, and usually people from the corps did not participate in these interviews. But I can't now confirm -- I can't say that we didn't have POWs and that we didn't interview them. This was the responsibility of the military security service. So in fact what I'm saying is we were not in a position to interview these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in certain cases POWs were interviewed. In what time frame was this and were you participating in such an interview, please?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That happened later on. I did not -- I wasn't personally involved in these interviews, but if we had a look at reports from 1994, we'd probably be able to find some information. If you have anything from that period, I'll be quite happy to comment on that information, but as far as I can remember, I did not have any such information, and I personally did not participate in interviews with POWs at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other witnesses have testified in front of this Chamber and stated that within the 3rd Corps and in the intelligence department of the 3rd Corps there was a so-called intelligence map. Can you explain what that intelligence map means as opposed to the ordinary map being in the operations centre of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Usually we would note down information that we had obtained on the map. The main difference is that we didn't make a note of information on our units apart from the zone of responsibility that had been assigned in certain orders, and naturally when noting such information, we tried to perform certain analysis. That was a sort of working map, so to speak. We would analyse certain information to try to make assessments to see whether assessments of an organ at a lower level fitted the larger picture that we had about the situation. That would be my explanation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on this intelligence map the positions of the VRS and the ABiH would be marked, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would the 3rd Corps Commander consult this map; on a daily basis, on a weekly basis?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Usually the commander would not consult the map at all. That was an internal map, and it was for the intelligence organ. The map in the operative centre had information that we provided when making the map, and naturally that was the map used. So there was no more information on that map than on the map in the operations centre. It was not necessary for the commander to come and use it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will have a break now since we have been working for an hour and a half. It's now twenty to six. We will resume at about 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall now resume, and we have approximately an hour left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I wanted to ask you about your intelligence on the presence of the HV in Central Bosnia. Can you tell us a little bit what you know about the presence of the HV in 1993 in Central Bosnia, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, the intelligence that we had, although I can't be very precise with that regard given the time that has lapsed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please hold on just a moment. Mr. Bourgon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Just to point out, ask for a clarification. Why is my learned friend asking questions about the presence of the army of the Republic of Croatia in Bosnia? The Chamber has already rendered a decision to that fact, and they said that the Prosecution can do that in order to establish a context but not in any other -- with any other objective. If -- if my learned friend is asking the question to establish a context it's okay, but not in any other case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have already rendered a decision on the nature of the conflict, whether it was an international conflict, and we said that you can do that in order to establish a context. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: We had certain intelligence. Truth be told, it was only on a few occasions when we had information about the presence of the HVO [as interpreted] citizens of the Republic of Croatia. I believe that in one report a reference is made to the members of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia. I wouldn't be able to give you any more specific detail unless you provide me with the specific report. I can't provide you with any more specific context. I believe that the initial information to that effect appeared in the Gornji Vakuf sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look in the Defence binder at tab number 11. This is DH579, tab number 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And for the record, I just want to state that there's an error in the transcript. On page 60, line 23, the witness testified "HV citizens," and here it says "HVO citizens."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe he can clarify. According to the English transcript, what did you say? Did you make a reference to the citizens of Croatia that arrived in that area? What did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said -- and I believe that this is a translation error. I made a reference to the citizens of the Republic of Croatia, and I also said that in one of the reports reference was made to members of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia. In both cases, these soldiers or policemen were citizens of the Republic of Croatia. So we had information about both the army members and the members of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the document DH579 in front of you? If you please look at the very last page, and can you confirm that this is your signature?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a report dated 16 of January, 1993. And can you look again on the last page of the B/C/S original. In the first main paragraph there you find the second column beginning with, and I'm citing the original words, "Takodje se." Do you find this? The second column, starting, then, with "Takodje se." The English original it's the bottom of page 2, the last column. You find it? Can you please read out this passage.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. It says: "Also we can confirm information about the stay of some 500 members of the Croatian army in the territory of Central Bosnia, 250 of whom are in Novi Travnik. They came from Split, Omis, and parts of Herzegovina. They are armed, most of them with infantry weapons."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having read this after some years now, does this refresh your recollection? Do you have anything to say to this?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Besides the fact that the reference is made to the parts of Herzegovina which is part of Bosnia and Herzegovina, if we're talking about the information which is very specific, this information was available at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And seeing your report after all these years, it states here, "Information was confirmed." From an intelligence perspective, what does this mean, it was confirmed?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This means that if certain information arrived for the second time of -- or from a different source, this information is confirmed. Information can be confirmed several times, but this is a minimum required for one piece of information to be confirmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please now look at tab 47 of the Defence binder, document DH1299. This is a document upon which you commented upon earlier. Can you look at the second paragraph. It talks about the Croatian army units there.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Am I supposed to read this or do you just want me to comment upon this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking whether you maybe recall the incident or whether this is new information. Then I would go on. The Croatian army is mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: I am not disproving things that were written. If you ask me whether I remember this particular information, I can only say that I've already said in general terms that there was information. I can't remember every particular document. Whether this information was subsequently confirmed, I don't know. It's hard to say. However, if this is something that I had at my disposal, this means that I had received it. In any case, whatever is written here it stays as it is. And I'm saying this primarily because there were indeed Croatian army units present in the -- these areas. Whether this particular information is correct, whether there were Croatian army units in these particular areas, it is very hard to say, you know. In the intelligence work, it is very rare when you can be absolutely certain that you have received a correct piece of intelligence. If this particular piece of intelligence is not confirmed from various sources after a certain period of time, and so on and so forth. It also depends on a particular source of information, because every source of information has its history.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You collected intelligence on the HVO and -- in Central Bosnia. Does this information or intelligence-gathering include also activities undertaken by the HVO in relation to permitting Mujahedin to pass -- coming from Croatia to pass through HVO-held parts into Central Bosnia? Did you come across such information?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first learn about the presence of Mujahedin in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no foundation for this question. It goes beyond the scope of the examination-in-chief. The witness has clearly said what his task was, what he was doing. In other Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. words, I believe that there is no foundation for this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The examination-in-chief never addressed the issue of the Mujahedin. The cross-examination, therefore, cannot address any issue that was not addressed in the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I respectfully request to continue this line of questioning because in the possession of the Prosecution are a few documents which show that indeed the witness had some knowledge about the Mujahedin, and according to Rule 90, the Prosecution is called upon to bring its case to the witnesses, and I'm prepared to show a particular document and ask from this document, stemming from this document, questions on the Mujahedin, if this helps. I was thinking to start with a very generic question to open up this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber will retire to deliberate on this issue and come back with a ruling. --- Break taken at 6.20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber has deliberated in order to render a decision whether the Prosecution can ask questions about the Mujahedin based on the document that has been disclosed to the Defence. To the extent that this document makes a reference to the witness, be it that he was its author or had something to do with it, the Prosecution is allowed to show the witness this document. And the Chamber has also decided that the witness was in charge of intelligence and he may be asked questions with regard to his professional activity in -- that had to do with the intelligence in the 3rd Corps. He may have been aware of the presence of foreigners in 1993, whether they were fighters or not fighters. Mr. Neuner, you have the floor. The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. With all due respect to my colleagues, if we are looking at the same document, this document does not make a reference to either Mujahedin or foreign fighters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're taking about the document that the Chamber does not have. That's why I said to the extent to which this document originates from the witness or the witness is mentioned herein. Maybe the Prosecution can explain the nature of this document that we don't know, that we are not aware of. If the Defence is right and if it's true that the Mujahedin is not mentioned in this document, why do you propose to show this document to the witness in the first place?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There is obviously a misunderstanding. In my previous intervention, I wasn't talking about having the new document being shown to the witness but in documents which are already in evidence or those which have been shown by the Defence in this binder to the witness and which carry the witness's signature and which relate to Mujahedin. I'm referring here to document DH580, which is in tab 10 of the Defence binder, and I'm also referring to Chamber Exhibit number 3 as a document which is in evidence which relates to the Mujahedin and which has a link. With Your Honours' permission, I would go on and show document DH580 briefly to the witness. Tab number 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you please look in the B/C/S version, on the very last page, the first column -- first of all, on the very last page you see your signature. Do you recognise your signature, please?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the first column, there is mentioning made of 500 Mujahedin in Kakanj. For the English version, this is page 2, under Section, and it says here "1:100.000 number 525." It's the first column. "Some of the men from Kakanj ..." it starts there. It's about eight lines down from "Section 1:100.000," mentioned on page 2. Do you, having read this passage some years after you have drawn up this report, do you recall anything about these Mujahedin or the allegations that Mujahedin would be in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: As I'm reading this document now, I can see that both pieces of intelligence were obtained through an interview with a Serb. I can't say who that person was. I don't believe that I was involved in that interview. However, the source of information says what he heard during his stay on two occasions in Serbia every time he returned via Kiseljak, and he had an opportunity to meet some people from Kakanj, people whom he knew, and it was these people that provided him with that information. If you want me to provide you with my opinion with this regard, I can say that I do not believe even to this very day after all that happened that this -- this is true. This is just a product of the propaganda that was present at the time, that reigned at the time. We listened to all the information regardless of its nature. This was not a matter of anyone's personal choice. It was not that you only listened to something that you liked as opposed to the things that you didn't like. People who are not objective, who are biased, cannot do this job. Whatever we received, we presented it in the form of information irrespective of the contents of this information. It is only if you put together all the available information that you can come up with a full picture, with a whole mosaic of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. If, with the assistance of the usher, a new document, document C3 could now please be shown to the witness. We have copies for everybody. This is tab 5 of the binder which you received. And there should be the handwritten notes at the end. On the middle it relates to a meeting on the 23rd of June. Do you find the handwritten notes, first of all?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you have find it.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [In English] This one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And it says Biljesevo in the upper right-hand corner. 23rd of June 1993, there was a meeting, and if you look at the participants of the meeting, you will find also your name. In the English version, it's on the bottom of page 1 where the participants of this meeting are mentioned. Do you find your name there or do you recall having been at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found my name in the part that mentions those in attendance, but I really can't remember. As we go through the document, I'll tell you what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also make a contribution to this meeting. First of all, the participants -- the meeting place. Do you recall the meeting place, having met at Biljesevo on the 23rd of June, 1993? You don't recall.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You make, according to the minutes, also a contribution. I think it is 01814208. Excuse me: 4209. There's your name mentioned there, the middle. In the English version, it's page number 7.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you now remember the meeting?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [In English] I really not, but I could comment at all information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, the Prosecution is interested in a contribution given by Mr. Amir Kubura on this meeting. Do you remember that Mr. Kubura made a contribution on -- first of all, do you remember that Mr. Kubura was at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't remember. I can't remember the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Mr. Kubura's Defence counsel is on his feet. You may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, we won't object since the witness has said he didn't remember, that he didn't remember what had been said, but the witness has just answered the question, so we withdraw our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Do proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have one more question relating to this meeting, or just an abstract question. Have you ever been at a meeting where the engagement of foreign nationals was discussed?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I assume if I show you the minutes which talk about this this will not help you? I'm just asking. I would be prepared to move on if you say you don't recall anything.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: You could do so. I could comment, but if I can't remember, there's nothing else I can say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In the English version it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'd just like to check something. Is my colleague saying that he has a document which shows that the witness participated or attended such a meeting? I don't know what the basis of his question is for asking the witness whether he attended a meeting or not. Is he fishing for something, or if the witness says, "I don't remember," is there a -- is there a document that mentions this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is a relevant objection. Could you be more clear, because some doubts have been raised. You mentioned conclusions of a meeting. Is this referred to in a document? Is it hypothesis? Could you be more clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It isn't a hypothesis. I was having in mind this particular meeting, but I didn't want to lead the witness to say that on this and this meeting the issue of Mujahedin was discussed, because my impression was he didn't recall. That's why I formulated the question abstract.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is indeed this meeting minutes. And if you please look at 01814203 where mention is made of Mr. Kubura and the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. He makes an intervention. In the English text it is page 4. If you please briefly read through this passage and look particularly at the proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I don't want to interrupt my learned colleague for no reason, but this question has already been asked and it has already been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It seems that the witness says that he can't remember this at all. Perhaps you could refresh his memory by showing him the conclusion, but that's not the witness's conclusion. Ask the witness if the conclusion on page 4 in the English translation corresponds to what he may have heard on that day or is there no more than he can say about the matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have heard the remark made by the Presiding Judge. Since you have refreshed your memory by reading through the intervention of the -- Mr. Kubura, and since you have read now the proposal, do you consider -- do you recall that this proposal was being discussed and that this is adequately reflected here in the minutes?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I really could not confirm anything. All I can say is that I don't remember this. I can provide you with comments on intelligence assessment that was made, I can confirm whether what was written down corresponded to the situation, but what you are referring to and with regard to the proposal, it says -- or that refers to engaging foreign nationals, well, I really don't remember that, and I could not say whether this is correct. If I can't remember something, I can't confirm it either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let -- let me please turn your attention to tab 2 of this binder, of this same binder. It's document P294. And can you please briefly indicate whether you recall that document, because your name is type signed on the end of this document. Can you please confirm that you recognise that document dated 10 December 1993.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I can't confirm that I remember this as the document was obviously issued by the intelligence organ and, as such, I can't confirm that it is a document from the intelligence organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your name is mentioned there as acting chief of intelligence security organ. Do you remember having received in December 1993 a reference from the Supreme Command Intelligence Administration, as it states here in the first paragraph, a request to provide intelligence information? Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I believe that I did receive that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In number 1, mentioning is made about the -- about foreign mercenaries in the BH theatre. Can you state what is meant by "foreign mercenaries in the BH theatre," please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That means anyone who was not a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina. They were foreign combatants. And in this particular case, mercenaries were probably men who went to the area and probably benefited in material terms from the fact because they were paid to fight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say they were paid to fight. Who paid them?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What foreign mercenaries did you think that the Supreme Command have in mind in December 1993 when it was requesting that information via you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I believe that they had in mind all those who were not citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All those who were not citizens. Do I take it this can include internationals fighting on behalf of the HVO, HOS, or also internationals fighting on the side of the -- to put it abstract, Muslim forces? To put it very abstract. What is meant by "foreign mercenaries"? Can you please explain.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I would agree with everything that you have just said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is -- what was the purpose to gather that information? It says in number 1, name, origin, number, type of unit, location of the unit's operation, commanding staff. What was the purpose of collecting that information?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I really don't know what the purpose was in that particular case. It was not the intelligence organ's task to focus on units that were part of the ABiH, but anything else might be a subject of interest, primarily Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. enemy forces. In this case, I don't know what the reason was. I don't know what the purpose was. And if we had a report, perhaps I could provide you with further comments. This is really something unusual, because this was not something that was within our field of activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You collected reconnaissance of VRS and HVO positions in 1993. Witnesses have testified in front of this Trial Chamber that also the Mujahedin were collecting such information. For example, witnesses testified that they were driving around in pick-up trucks and reconnoitering positions. Were you aware that in 1993, in the 3rd Corps area, such reconnaissance was collected?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, for my learned colleague to put such questions to the witness and to refer to certain witnesses who have testified before this Tribunal that the Mujahedin gathered information, this is an inappropriate way to cross-examine the witness, and so far the witness has not testified about the Mujahedin. We don't understand the reasons for which the Prosecution has now moved on to another subject. Up until now, the Prosecution has been referring to foreign mercenaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We were speaking about foreign mercenaries. Why are you establishing a link between foreign mercenaries and the Mujahedin given that the witness is not familiar with the situation? He didn't provide any precise information, and it would perhaps have been better to ask him if he had seen white vehicles, white Japanese vehicles circulating, and I won't mention the name of these vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any white vehicles, meant by certain persons of foreign origin, who were driving around in the 3rd Corps area of responsibility and were looking at certain positions of the adversaries? Did you see in 1993 such vehicles?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I did see a white vehicle or white vehicles used by foreigners, but I was never able to see -- or I never saw such vehicles carrying out reconnaissance. But to try and facilitate this matter, I can claim with full responsibility that none of the foreigners used for intelligence in the 3rd Corps organ, which is where I was and this is what I could have had information about, well, I don't know whether this might assist you or not, but I never attended any meetings with any foreign mercenaries or any foreigners involved in intelligence within the 3rd Corps or involved in operations or in any other matters. The only people that I had contact with, and they also had white vehicles - perhaps they weren't Japanese ones - the only people that I had contact with were from international organisations. You can continue to ask me questions, but I want to answer your question. I don't want you to think that I'm trying to avoid giving you a certain answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just asking you as a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you as an intelligence officer at the time, the very fact that individuals were gathering intelligence or information within your area of responsibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my learned friend has already pre-judged certain matters. Awhile ago he was referring to certain witnesses, and now he has mentioned something that has been established as a fact. But I believe that you will have the final decision as to the weight to give to the evidence before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The witness never said these individuals were circulating to gather information. This is the first time that we have heard this from the Prosecution. I never heard -- I have never heard about individuals circulating in vehicles to collect information. If this is what you claim, you probably have a basis for this claim, but we're not aware of the basis. But you could rephrase your question as the witness said that he did see vehicles circulating, but whether these individuals were just driving around, were they trying out the vehicle, did they want to just buy Coca-Cola, I don't know. But to say that vehicles were circulating to gather information, well this is quite an affirmation. But ask the witness to answer the question since he said he was ready to answer your questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've heard the intervention of His Honour the Presiding Judge. These vehicles, the white vehicles, the pick-ups, did you have any knowledge in 1993 what the activities performed from these or in these vehicles, what these activities were about, whether people were standing on the flatbed of these vehicles just for their own pleasure or whether they were engaging in some kind of activity, observe certain things? Do you know -- did you have any understanding on what these vehicles -- what the purpose of driving around these vehicles was?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: No. I never saw anyone driving around for reconnaissance purposes. I never saw someone in a white vehicle in vicinity of -- I don't know, the lines or some location from which reconnaissance would be carried out. If I saw them, that would probably be somewhere in town. So I really wouldn't know. I really don't know why these individuals were using those vehicles. They were probably just driving around. But what you have referred to, what you have mentioned, is something that I personally did not observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. I would have only the new document to show to this witness, and I noted -- I see my friend -- learned friend on their feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have a document to refresh the witness's memory or to test the witness's credibility? What category would this document fall into?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It would be a memory-refreshing document, and it is signed by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If my learned colleague could say why he wants to refresh the witness's memory, I would be grateful. Does this document have to do with white vehicles or something else? I apologise, but if the document is to be shown, it is necessary to provide a basis. It's necessary to state why the witness's memory should be refreshed or why it's necessary to discredit the witness. The fact that the witness has signed the document doesn't mean anything in itself from a legal point of view. This is not a reason to show such a document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I object to this document at the beginning of this last section. This document doesn't refer to the Mujahedin or to foreign mercenaries, and it doesn't refer to anything that was -- any issues raised in the course of the examination-in-chief or in the course of the cross-examination conducted by my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have heard the two objections, so could you now clarify the matter? This is a document that was drafted by the witness or contradicts something the witness says? Could you clarify the matter and provide us with more information on this new document? And I would also like to point out that it's 7.00 p.m. now. We could continue to midnight, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document relates to an issue which is important for the Prosecution's case in the sense that it shows the presence of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade -- of members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in the -- can I maybe ask the witness to leave the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This document relates to the presence of the 7th Muslim -- of members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in the Bila Valley in May 1993, and before I would respectfully request to show this document to the witness, the Prosecution would be prepared to ask -- to lay a foundation and to ask some introductory questions. However, it's -- it's a detail which is mentioned here in a document signed by this witness, and it's such a particular detail that it will probably be necessary to refresh the witness's recollection about this event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you well, there's a document signed by the witness that speaks about the 7th Brigade, but how are you going -- proposing to make a link between the 7th Brigade and the Mujahedin? I believe this is the essence of the objection that was put forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It is not intended to make any link between the two. The prior line of questioning has ceased. It was just a last attempt of the Prosecution try to finish the cross-examination today. So it is not intended to make any link between the previous questioning and this questioning now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you would simply like to ask the witness whether he has signed the document, whether it is a mistake that the 7th Brigade is mentioned as the troops attacking a village? Is that what you want to ask the witness? The Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I believe that at the end of the working day, at 7.00 in the evening, my learned friend opens an issue that was not the subject of the examination-in-chief or the cross-examination. I object to this issue being opened because it goes beyond the scope of today's examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Defence says that the examination-in-chief did not open the issue of the 7th Brigade, which is true, and that the subject that you wish to address has nothing to do with the questions that were -- have been put to the witness so far. Why do you want to show the witness this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to show this document to the witness because it was authored by this witness, and the Prosecution hopes that the witness is in a position to elaborate on a document which he has produced 12 or -- ten or 12 years ago and can elucidate that fact or what he knows about the presence of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in the Bila Valley in 1993. And it was always the Prosecution's position that members of this unit were there at the time, an issue which is contested. And since this witness has authored the document, the Prosecution is of the position that it has, according to Rule 90, the possibility to ask such a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much more time would you be needing?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would simply ask two questions at the beginning in abstract about this event. If the witness does remember right away, I will ask him to elaborate and we will not even show him the document. If he doesn't remember, I will just show him the document and ask him. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence, as far as the re-examination is concerned, do you know how much time you will need? Mr. Bourgon nods. So you do have re-examination. Maybe it would be best if we continued tomorrow. Mr. Bourgon nods his head. Maybe it would be best to continue tomorrow, otherwise we may stay here until 8.00 or 9.00 this evening. Can you please bring the witness into the courtroom and we will explain to him why he needs to return tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, I will have to ask you to come back tomorrow. It is ten by -- past seven. We are already ten minutes after the scheduled time. The Prosecution still needs another ten minutes, but the Defence are going to have some additional questions. We cannot, therefore, finish today. That's why we will have to ask you to come back tomorrow afternoon. Unfortunately, this is the only way. So you have to stay one day longer. Please come back tomorrow at quarter past two for the conclusion of your testimony. And let me just tell you that since you have taken the solemn declaration, you are not supposed to talk to either the Defence or the Prosecution. We wish you a good rest this evening. We shall see you back at quarter past two. We are going to render this decision about the contested issue, and we will resume at quarter past two. I invite everybody to come back at quarter past two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
